Which battle I meant, Muramasa seemed to understand without requiring the explanation.

I placed the fragment in her hand and moved a little away.
The one who had left us had left words also. They came back to me.

—Kageaki Minato cannot defeat Hikaru Minato.

But.
A hero who protects the world can kill a demon king who destroys it.

理解した様子だった。

　しかし。
　世界を守る英雄は、世界を壊す魔王を殺せる。

Born as living armor. Human, and not human. A tool, and not a tool. I thought of the one who had put the key to destruction into such a world.

The war between Rokuhara and the occupation forces. The chaos after it.

Heavy words.
More than ten years' worth of them, coming out in that apology.

I knew what answer I had to give.

This short talk.
This talk which had to happen.
What I must say at the end of it—I knew.

One sentence only, and it hurt to say it.
Even so.

en.html:
My adoptive father turned and went away.

His steps were heavy, as if old age had arrived all at once and put its weight in his feet.
To his retreating back, I bowed deeply. Once only.

I closed my eyes and let the understanding settle inside.

—That man.

The man called Akitaka Minato.
Now he had truly gone.

It felt as though a heavy load had been put on my back.
And at the same time, as though I had shaken something off.

Only—this was right.

That was what I thought.

ja.html:
重い荷を背負ったようでもあり。
　逆に、何かを振り切ったようでもあり。

　ただ――これで正しいのだ、と。

　そう思った。
